Subject: Initial redlines + evidence request for onboarding

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the call earlier. QuantumData is aligned on the economics but legal flagged a few items in the Order Form / MSA related to output title and model retrain permissions. We attached a single PDF with inline redlines (QD-OrderForm-v3-redlines.pdf). Major asks from our counsel: 

- Clarify whether outputs we generate are assignable to QuantumData (we prefer clear output title).
- Confirm what data Redwood keeps and whether customer content may be used to improve models (we need an explicit opt-out or a no-training clause).
- Evidence request: by procurement policy, we require a short packet showing telemetry/retention controls and SOC2 or equivalent artifacts for security review.

Can your team provide a point person for legal + a timeline for: redline reconciliation, evidence pack, and a final Order Form? We need to close procurement by 12/20 to hit our Q4 deployment window.

Attachments: QD-OrderForm-v3-redlines.pdf (pdf, 620KB)

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds

Ava —

Appreciate the redlines and the timeline. Quick read-through and initial commitments below: 

- Output ownership: we typically grant customers broad usage rights and, for most standard SaaS integrations, we do not claim downstream ownership. For cases where customers want explicit assignment of title, that requires legal review (and—depending on scope—possible Order Form language). We can propose a permissive assignment clause or a limited license; will confirm with legal.

- Training/data use: Redwood’s default: customer content is not used to train any models across tenants unless customer opts in. We can add explicit opt-out language or a training exemption in the Order Form.

- Evidence pack: Kimberly will own the SOC2/telemetry packet. Ben will help with retention/telemetry language and provide a short summary of what logs & audit trails we can include. Monica can coordinate procurement handoff and DocuSign routing once redlines are resolved.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Kimberly and Ben to draft a short evidence ZIP and a paragraph we can insert into the Order Form clarifying retention and masking controls (ETA: 48 hrs).
2) Legal to propose two options for output rights: (A) assignment clause that requires review; (B) explicit customer-owned outputs + no-training carveout — we’ll aim to provide clean language for both (ETA: 3 business days).
3) Demo the evidence pack to QuantumData’s security lead if they want a quick walkthrough (15–20 mins).

We’ll prioritize the 12/20 procurement closure. Looping legal and security now.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

Hi all —

I reviewed QuantumData's redlines. Short answers and attachments below.

1) Training/use: Confirming Redwood default is non-consent — customer data is not used to train our public models. For customers that want training enabled, it’s opt-in and captured in the Order Form. We can add a sentence: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve or retrain any Redwood or third-party models unless Customer provides written opt-in."

2) Output title: Customer outputs are normally licensed to the customer for their use. Title assignment is unusual for consumptive outputs (we typically offer a perpetual, worldwide license). If QuantumData needs assignment of title to outputs for re-sale or productization, that is a commercial exception and we need Exec/legal approval.

3) Evidence pack: attached egress of the checklist and a short redactable artifact list. Items we can provide immediately: high-level SOC2 status, retention windows, audit-log sample, and an architectural diagram showing tenant isolation. We cannot share raw production logs; we can share aggregated/obfuscated examples and a signed attestation. See attached: evidence-pack-logs-and-soc2.txt (stub).

Requested items from QuantumData to speed process: 
- The specific legal language they want for "assignment" vs the license path (if they have preferred clause text).
- Security contact to schedule a 15-min walkthrough (email + timezone).

I will prepare the 48-hr pack and the two-orderform language options Logan mentioned. If QuantumData prefers immediate no-training language, we can surface that as the default in the next draft.

Attachments: evidence-pack-logs-and-soc2.txt (text, 12KB)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance & Trust | Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Logan —

Thanks — that helps a lot. Quick replies from our side: 

- Security lead is Ben H. (ben.hughes@quantumdata.ai) — available Thu 12/10 10:00 PT for a 20-min review.
- QuantumData legal prefers a clause that explicitly assigns "exclusive rights to outputs generated by the services" for the first-party productization use case; they also asked for an alternate path where Redwood grants an "exclusive, transferrable license instead of full title assignment".
